title: Responder roundup and carryover — Apr 05–09, 2027
content:
TL;DR:
Week highlight: two transient incidents (Apr 06 and Apr 08) caused elevated tail latency for hosted-api small-models. Error budget dipped to 62% for /generate-prod route but recovered after rolling a minor runtime patch and temporarily reducing max batch size for the affected model pool.

High-level timeline (local times, PDT):
- 2027-04-06 10:18 — First reports: intermittent 500s and 2–3s tail latencies on /generate-prod (small models pool). Alert: P99 latency spike (>1200ms) and increased 5xx count. (INC-4217 opened)
- 2027-04-06 10:28 — On-call triage: scaled pool by +20% capacity (quick autoscale). Latency improved but intermittent errors persisted.
- 2027-04-06 11:05 — Mitigation: reverted recent kernel selection change (rolling restart of 6 nodes). Error rate dropped; incident closed 11:30 with postmortem flag.
- 2027-04-08 03:12 — Night shift: repeat of elevated tail latency, different symptom: KV cache thrashing observed causing CPU spikes on a subset of nodes.
- 2027-04-08 03:40 — Temporary mitigation: reduce per-worker max_batch_tokens from 512 -> 384 for small-model config; enabled extra KV cache warming for affected shards.
- 2027-04-08 06:00 — Morning follow-up: rolled out runtime patch (PR #2140) that gates an aggressive cache-eviction heuristic. Full recovery confirmed by 07:20.

Incident notes / root cause hypotheses:
- Apr 06: regression introduced by kernel-selection heuristic that chose a suboptimal execution kernel under specific sequence-length distribution; resulted in resource contention on some GPU models. Patch reverted.
- Apr 08: separate but related — KV cache eviction policy was overly aggressive under low-memory pressure combination with new batching pattern; led to cache misses, CPU overhead, and tail latency. Patch addressed the eviction threshold; longer-term fix is to add per-model cache pressure signals to the scheduler.
- Both incidents surfaced the same class of problem: heuristics that are tuned for median workload but brittle at the tails (bursting patterns).

SLO snapshot (snapshot time: 2027-04-09 08:00 PDT):
- Route: /generate-prod (small-models pool)
  - Availability (30d): 99.95%
  - P99 latency (30d rolling): 820ms (target: <800ms) — slight breach window observed Apr 06/08
  - Error budget remaining: 62% (was 88% two weeks ago)

Operational observations and trends:
- P99 drift tied to traffic bursts from two customers using long-context chat sessions after a client-side update. Need to coordinate with growth/CS for throttling/coordination flags.
- Autoscaler handled throughput but didn't prevent micro-thrashing during kernel-selection transitions; consider a short cooldown on kernel swaps.
- Night-shift responders executed mitigations cleanly, but post-incident runbook steps (evidence capture, artifact tagging) were inconsistently done.

Runbook gaps identified:
- No clear checklist for 'kernel-selection rollback' — current playbooks assume full node restart; create a compact rollback play that minimizes churn.
- KV cache telemetery is sparse: need per-shard eviction counters and a heatmap dashboard for correlating eviction spikes with latency.
- Lack of a standard 'temporary config' rubric (max_batch_tokens changes) and a rollback TTL — add a templated change with automatic revert if metrics worsen.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Aisha: Draft kernel-rollback playbook (short checklist + commands) and land in Confluence. ETA: 2027-04-16.
- Jonas: Instrument per-shard cache eviction counters (export to prometheus) + add heatmap dashboard. ETA: 2027-04-23.
- Priya: Add a gating policy in the autoscaler to avoid kernel re-selection within 5m of a previous selection (cooldown). Small RFC + prototype. ETA: 2027-04-30.
- Marco: Coordination note to Growth/CS about customer traffic bursts; request throttling feature flag for heavy-context sessions. ETA: 2027-04-12.
- Ellen: Create a 'temporary config' run template in infra repo and add an automatic TTL revert. ETA: 2027-04-20.
- Team: Run a tabletop exercise focusing on tail-latency incidents with kernel/cache interactions. Proposed date: 2027-04-28. Organizer: Aisha.

On-call handoff (carryover items for next shift):
- Keep an eye on small-models pool P99 and eviction counters (dash: SRE > KV-eviction-heatmap).
- Do not apply kernel-selection heuristic changes without a canary in dedicated canary pool.
- Temporary config 'max_batch_tokens=384' should auto-revert by 2027-04-10 12:00 unless extended with a postmortem-approved PR. (Owner: Ellen)
- Follow up on INC-4217: postmortem draft needed (assigned: Jonas).

Meeting notes / standup snippets (raw):
- Priya: "noticed odd CPU spikes on nodes with high cache churn — we should add an eviction metric ASAP."
- Jonas: "postmortem will include sequence-length distribution sampling; found skewed longs from two customers."
- Marco: "can we add a temporary routing rule to steer suspected heavy sessions to dedicated pools?"
- Ellen: "I'll put config TTL into a small infra PR today — aim for deploy tomorrow morning."

Decision log (quick):
- Roll back kernel-selection heuristic (Apr 06).
- Patch eviction heuristic to be conservative by default and expose tuning knobs (Apr 08).
- Temporary decrease of max_batch_tokens for small-models to reduce KV pressure (Apr 08).

Parking lot / questions to be resolved:
- How to automate detection of 'bursting customers' and signal Growth for mitigation? (possible: metrics-based alerts + account tags)
- Long-term: add per-customer rate-limiting at the router layer vs. per-pool throttling. Trade-offs: UX vs. SLO isolation.
- Investigate model-specific cache profiles (are some models inherently high-eviction?).

Notes to self / informal:
- We should capture a short screencast of the command sequence for rollback (new hires + oncall).
- Consider a short 'SRE cookbook' page with common quick mitigations (scale, reduce batch, revert kernel) and exact CLI commands.
- Gratitude callout: night responders were solid; no major customer impact beyond transient errors.

Next sync: Weekly ops review + tabletop on 2027-04-28 (add to calendar).

Files to attach to postmortem: incident timeline export, perf traces, PR #2140 diff, autoscaler logs, KV eviction histogram (raw).

Unresolved: postmortem owner needs to add a timeline with exact node ids — Jonas to collect by 2027-04-12.

END OF NOTES

(Informal / working doc: will be cleaned and converted into an official postmortem + runbook additions once action items are in progress.)
